title: The Delhi Attic Where HCL Began on Calculator Money
conflicts: Founders: six (Rediff, Swarajya, Dataquest) vs eight (Outlook); the story names six and gives no count. Capital: Rs 1.87 lakh (Dataquest 2003) vs Nadar's own account of $16,000 savings for the calculator company and Rs 20 lakh for HCL with a quarter from the UP government; Nadar's figures used, attributed. Microcomp dated 1975 (Dataquest) vs founders quitting in summer 1976 (Rediff); no year given for Microcomp. Nadar's age 30 (press) vs 31 (himself); his figure used.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'bootstrapped' to 'mixed' because the Uttar Pradesh government supplied a quarter of HCL's starting capital through the joint venture. The main source is Nadar's 2006 Knowledge at Wharton interview, which also gives the attic description that matches the barsati reported by Swarajya, Outlook and Business Today.
